IN THE HIGH COURT OF KERALA AT ERNAKULAM

 PRESENT:

 THE HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE ANTONY DOMINIC
 &
 THE HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE P.D.RAJAN

 FRIDAY, THE 25TH DAY OF OCTOBER 2013/3RD KARTHIKA, 1935

 Mat.Appeal.No. 55 of 2011 ( )
 ------------------------------
 AGAINST THE ORDER/JUDGMENT IN OPDIV 1267/2009 of FAMILYCOURT,KOTTAYAM
 AT ETTUMANOOR DATED 28-10-2010

APPELLANT(S)/PETITIONER:
---------------------------------------------

 BIJU @ ABRAHAM,
 AGED 35, S/O. JOSE ABRAHAM,KONNACKAL HOUSE,
 PANACHEPPALLY KARA, PANACHEPPALLY P.O.
 KOOVAPPALLY VILLAGE, KANJIRAPPALLY TALUK,
 NOW WORKING AT BIJU JAMES, WEETHERFORD OIL TOOL
 LTD., P.O. BOX. 4627, JEBEL ALI, U.A.E.KOTTAYAM DISTRICT.

 BY ADV. SRI.GEORGE POONTHOTTAM

RESPONDENT(S)/RESPONDENT:
--------------------------------------------------

 RENI @ CLARAMMA, AGED 31 YEARS,
 D/O. JOY JOSEPH, KOLLAMPARAMBIL HOUSE, CHENAPPADY KARA
 KANJIRAPPALLY TALUK, KOTTAYAM DISTRICT - 686 507.


 THIS MATRIMONIAL APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 25-10-2013,
 ALONG WITH MA. 56/2011, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE
 FOLLOWING:




acd



 ANTONY DOMINIC & P.D. RAJAN, JJ.
 -------------------------------------------
 Mat. Appeal Nos.55/2011 & 56/2011
 ----------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 25th day of October, 2013

 JUDGMENT
ANTONY DOMINIC,J.

These appeals are filed against the common judgment

passed by the Family Court, Kottayam in O.P.(Div)No.1267/2009

and O.P.No.56/2010.

2. O.P.(Div)No.1267/2009 was filed by the appellant

husband seeking divorce on the ground of desertion and cruelty

as provided under Section 10(ix) and (x) of the Indian Divorce

Act 1869 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act' for short).

O.P.No.56/2010 was filed by the respondent wife, seeking return

of 28 sovereigns of gold ornaments, Rs.1 lakh PF amount, steel

almirah and certificates from the appellant. These cases were

jointly tried and on behalf of the husband, PWs 1 to 4 were

examined and on behalf of the wife, Rws 1 to 3 were examined.

Exts.A1 to A3 and B1 and B2 were marked by both sides. The

Family Court by the common judgment rendered on 28th October

Mat. Appeal No.55/10 & con.case 2

2010 dismissed O.P.(Div)No.1267/2009 and partly allowed

O.P.No.56/2010. The counter claim raised by the appellant

was also rejected. It is in these circumstances, the appellants

have filed these appeals

3. Insofar as Mat. Appeal No.55/2011 arising out of

O.P.(Div)No.1267/2010 is concerned, as already stated by us,

the grounds urged are desertion and cruelty.
4. Insofar as plea of desertion is concerned, Section 10

(ix) of the Act permits divorce on this ground, if it is proved

that the respondent has deserted the petitioner for at least two

years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition.

In this case, the marriage between the parties was on

30.1.2002 and a female child was born in the wedlock.

According to the appellant husband, the respondent had gone

to her house for delivery on 15.4.2005. His case is that at the

time of her departure, she had made a declaration that she did

not intend to return to the matrimonial home. He also averred

that thereafter, various efforts were made by him and that in

spite of it, the wife was adamant not to rejoin to him. He also

has narrated the mediation efforts allegedly initiated at his

instance when also according to him, the wife turned down his

Mat. Appeal No.55/10 & con.case 3

request to reunite in the matrimonial home. It is on this basis,

he pleads that the wife deserted him, entitling him to a decree

of divorce on that ground.

5. However, the case of the wife was that, despite

cruelty that was meted out her by her husband as also his

people, she was keen to maintain and restore the matrimonial

relationship. It was also her case that though she was always

willing to reunite with the appellant husband, the appellant

husband was adamant not to restore the matrimonial

relationship.

6. In her proof affidavit, she has specifically averred

that after the marriage of the brother of the appellant

husband, which was held on 31.3.2008, she stayed in the

house of the appellant husband and that such reunion was on

the instruction of the Priest to whom the appellant husband

had made a complaint against the respondent. She also has

averred that during this period, the appellant husband had

gone abroad and that she had, for some time gone and stayed

with her parents. She further averred that when the appellant

husband returned from abroad, again, they stayed together for

another one month and that thereafter also the appellant

Mat. Appeal No.55/10 & con.case 4

husband and his relatives treated her with cruelty, which

compelled her to return to her parental home. According to

her, it was thereafter in August 2008, she got an employment

in Delhi and left to join her employment.

7. We have gone through the examination of the wife,

who was examined as RW1. On the above claims made by her

in her proof affidavit, there is no cross examination at all. If

that be so, we have to proceed on the basis that her evidence

to the above effect was accepted by the appellant husband. If

that be the case, the situation that emerges is that the

desertion, if any, that is prior to 31.3.2008 stands condoned

by the appellant husband by restoration of the matrimonial

relationship.

8. Moreover, the petition, which was filed before the

Family Court on 2.12.2009 also did not satisfy the two years

period of desertion specified in Section 10(ix) of the Act.

Therefore, we are unable to accept the case of desertion

pleaded by the appellant husband and hold that the Family

Court was justified in rejecting the case of desertion urged by

the husband.

9. Insofar as the cruelty pleaded by the appellant

Mat. Appeal No.55/10 & con.case 5

husband is concerned, in order to succeed on the ground of

cruelty, Section 10 (x) of the Act provides that the petitioner

should prove that he was treated with such cruelty as to cause

reasonable apprehension in the mind of the petitioner that it

would be harmful or injurious to him to live with the

respondent.

10. Insofar as the case of cruelty urged by the appellant

husband is concerned, the pleadings as disclosed in the

petition would show that there is not even an allegation of any

specific incident of cruelty and on the other hand, all

allegations levelled by him are general and vague. Therefore,

on his own pleadings, this is not a case where a Court of law

could have accepted the case of cruelty pleaded by the

husband to allow a divorce on that ground.

11. Therefore, this ground urged by the appellants also

could not have been accepted . For these reasons, we uphold

the judgment of the Family Court dismissing O.P.(Div)

No.1267/2009.

12. Now what remains is Mat. Appeal No.56/2011 filed

against O.P.No.56/2010. The decree passed by the Family

Court requires the appellant husband to repay Rs.1 lakh with

Mat. Appeal No.55/10 & con.case 6

7% interest, return 20 sovereigns of gold ornaments or its

approximate value of Rs.2,60,000/-. The Family Court was

also ordered 7% interest on the amount payable. Further the

Court also directed the appellant husband to return the

almirah or its value of Rs.3,000/-.

13. Insofar as the almirah is concerned, the appellant

husband himself admitted that the same is available and that

he is willing to return the same.

14. Insofar as Rs.1 lakh and 20 sovereigns of gold

ornaments is concerned, the case of the respondent wife was

that she was paid patrimony of Rs.2 lakh and that utilising

Rs.1 lakh, 20 sovereigns of gold ornaments were purchased

and that the same was entrusted to the 2nd appellant, the

father-in-law. According to her, the gold ornaments were

misappropriated and therefore, she was entitled to get it

returned from he appellants.

15. On the other hand, the appellants contended that

out Rs.2 lakhs entrusted as patrimony, expending

Rs.1,23,000/-, they had purchased 20 sovereigns of gold and

that the same was always with the respondent wife. According

to them, at the time when she went to Pune, where the couple

Mat. Appeal No.55/10 & con.case 7

were residing, she had entrusted the ornaments with her

mother. In other words, the appellants denied the case of

entrustment of the ornaments set up by the wife.

16. Thus the fact that Rs.2 lakh was paid as patrimony

is admitted. Further, the purchase of 20 sovereigns of gold

ornaments is also admitted. The Family Court on evidence

also found that only Rs.1 lakh could have been spent for

purchasing 20 sovereigns of gold ornaments. This conclusion

is based on the market value of gold then prevailing. There is

nothing before us to indicate that this conclusion of the Family

Court is erroneous.

17. Now the question is whether the appellants in Mat.

Appeal No.56/2011 are liable to return 20 sovereigns of gold

ornaments.

18. As far as this issue is concerned, this liability arises

only if it is proved by the wife that the ornaments in question

were entrusted to the appellants. Insofar as this aspect of the

matter is concerned, evidence is totally lacking and there is

also no conclusive finding by the Family Court on this aspect.

19. For that reason, we are unable to sustain the Family

Court required the appellants to return 20 sovereigns of gold

Mat. Appeal No.55/10 & con.case 8

ornaments. Therefore, the decree passed by the Family

Court, Kottayam in O.P.No.56/2010 to the extent it requires

the appellants to return 20 sovereigns of gold ornaments or its

then market value of Rs.2,60,000/- with 7% interest from the

date of the suit, is set aside.

20. In all other respects, the judgment will stand

confirmed.

Accordingly, the Mat. Appeal No.56/2011 is disposed of

and Mat. Appeal N.55/2011 will stand dismissed.

ANTONY DOMINIC, JUDGE




 P.D. RAJAN, JUDGE

acd

Mat. Appeal No.55/10 & con.case 9
Mat. Appeal No.55/10 & con.case 10
